title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, Risk & Exceptions
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance requirements and operational playbooks for RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC gates, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and the risk & exceptions process. It is intended for engineering, security, and compliance stakeholders.

1) Overview
- Purpose: Provide a single-source-of-truth for access control, logging, data handling, and evidence collection so customers and auditors can validate controls and engineers can follow repeatable procedures.
- Scope: Applies to hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments; control plane and customer-facing services; non-production and production environments unless specified.
- Owners: Security (policy definition), Eng-SRE (operational implementation), Eng-Platform (IAM integration), Legal (compliance requirements).

2) RBAC & Authentication
Heading: Principles
- Least privilege by default; role-based groups mapped to job functions.
- Separation of duties for privileged roles (no single individual with full prod/admin and finance access).
- Strong authentication: enterprise SSO (Okta), SAML/OIDC for services, MFA required for all human accounts.

Role Catalog (high level):
| Role | Typical Members | Permissions Summary | Owner | Review Cadence |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| viewer | auditors, analysts | read-only dashboards, logs | eng-platform | 90 days |
| developer | product & infra devs | repo access, non-prod deploy | eng-dev | 90 days |
| service-account | CI/CD, monitoring | token-limited service actions | eng-sre | 30 days |
| infra-admin | infra engineers | create/destroy infra (non-customer data) | eng-infra | 30 days |
| prod-admin | small set of oncall engineers | production config changes | eng-sre/security | 30 days |

Assignment and provisioning:
1. Provisioning requests via HR + Okta group SCIM sync or the internal Access Request portal. 2. All requests require a business justification and an approver (team lead). 3. Time-bound access for third parties and contractors. 4. Emergency/break-glass flows use temporary elevating tokens audited and automatically revoked after 8 hours.

Access reviews and attestations:
- Quarterly access review for all privileged roles. 30-day review for infra-admin and prod-admin. Results recorded in the evidence repo (/evidence/access-reviews/YYYY-MM).

3) Audit Logging
Goals:
- Capture who/what/when/where for sensitive operations (auth events, config changes, model deployments, secret access, role grants).
- Ensure tamper-evident storage and timely delivery to log storage.
SLOs and thresholds:
- Ingestion latency: 99th percentile < 60s for critical audit events.
- Log availability SLO: 99.9% 30d window.
- Integrity: daily immutability checkpoints stored in S3 with checksum and KMS envelope encryption.

Log sources and retention:
- Identity/auth logs: Okta (retained 1 year in primary, archived up to 7 years for enterprise customers).
- Application audit logs: produced by auth-service, control-plane-api, deployment-service -> forwarded to Splunk/Datadog and backed up to encrypted S3. Default retention 1 year; enterprise retention configurable up to 7 years.
- System & infra logs: Cloud Audit Logs / CloudTrail retained 90 days in hot storage; archived to long-term bucket for 7 years where required by contract.

Format and metadata (standard fields):
- timestamp, event_id, service, environment, principal_id, principal_type, action, target_resource, resource_id, outcome (success/fail), request_id, trace_id, raw_payload (if permitted).

Log protection:
- All logs encrypted at rest (KMS/HSM) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). Access to logs limited via RBAC and logged for auditing. Immutable backup snapshots taken nightly.

4) Data Residency & Retention
Policy summary:
- Hosted API default region: US (multi-region failover). Customers may select EU residency for personal data. Private and Dedicated deployments follow customer network/region constraints.
- Data classification: PII, customer_model_weights, telemetry, business-data. Each classification maps to allowed regions and retention windows in the Controls table below.

Controls mapping table:
| Data Class | Default Region | Default Retention | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| PII | EU/US (per customer choice) | 7 years (or per contract) | security/legal | Subject to GDPR/CCPA rules |
| Customer Model Artifacts | Customer-chosen region | Customer-specified (default 1 year) | eng-private-deployments | Private deployment may impose stricter retention |
| Telemetry (aggregated) | US | 2 years | eng-platform | Redacted PII, used for analytics |

Retention enforcement:
- Automated retention jobs run daily to purge expired data using immutable deletion markers. Deletions produce an audit event.
- Retention exceptions require documented approval and are time-bound (see Risk & Exceptions).

5) Secure SDLC (security gates & automation)
Stages and gates:
- Design: Threat model required for services exposing customer data or public endpoints. Owner: engineering team with security reviewer.
- Implement: SCA (software composition analysis) scans on PRs, static analysis on critical repos.
- Test: Automated unit + integration tests, DAST for public endpoints, secret scanning. Build must be green and pass policy checks to be promoted.
- Release: Pre-release checklist includes dependency CVE threshold (no critical unmitigated), infra change review (PR), canary rollout plan, and compliance checklist.
- Post-release: Automated monitoring (behavioral/telemetry) and a 7-day smoke window for staged rollouts.

Automation & gates tools:
- CI: Buildkite/GitHub Actions with policy enforcement.
- SCA: Snyk/OSS-Fuzz alerts integrated into PR.
- Secrets: git-secrets + pre-commit checks.

Ownership and evidence:
- Security review artifacts (threat models, SCA results, PR approvals) are stored under /evidence/sdlc/{repo}/{release} and referenced in the release ticket.

6) Incident Response - Security Procedures
Objectives:
- Contain, eradicate, and recover while preserving forensic evidence and meeting notification obligations.

On-call & escalation:
1. Detection: Alerts routed to eng-sre and security oncall via PagerDuty. 2. Triage: Severity assigned (sev1- sev4) with initial triage in 15 minutes for Sev1. 3. Incident lead assigned and timeline started.

Immediate steps (high level):
1. Triage and scope: capture affected services, impacted customers, and initial indicators. 2. Preserve evidence: snapshot relevant hosts, collect logs from central log store (avoid modifying hosts). 3. Containment: revoke compromised credentials, rotate keys, apply network ACLs. 4. Eradication & recovery: patch, rebuild from known-good artifacts, and validate. 5. Postmortem: 72-hour interim summary and a full postmortem within 30 days.

Forensic guidance:
- Use forensics playbook for VM and container snapshots (see /confluence/forensics-playbook). All evidence chain-of-custody must be documented.
- Communications: Security coordinates customer and regulator notifications with Legal and Customer Success.

7) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Evidence types:
- Config snapshots, access-review artifacts, log archives, change approvals, threat models, test results, and contractual residency directives.
Workflow to produce evidence for audits:
1. Request intake: GRC or auditor opens ticket in Jira with scope. 2. Triage & owner map: Security maps controls to owners and artifacts. 3. Evidence pull: Owners export artifacts (signed PDFs, log extracts, CSVs) to the evidence repo. 4. Validation: Security performs a completeness check. 5. Delivery: Provide signed archive and an index manifest.
Checklist for common artifacts:
- Access review CSV with approvers and timestamps.
- Audit log extracts for requested window in JSON/NDJSON with checksums.
- Architecture and threat model PDFs stamped with reviewer signatures.

Evidence retention and protection:
- Evidence archives kept for a minimum of 3 years by default, 7 years where contractually required. Archives are stored encrypted with restricted access and audited retrieval.

8) Risk & Exceptions
Exception process:
1. Submit request: Owner files an exception ticket in the Risk Tracker with justification, scope, compensating controls, and TTL. 2. Triage: Security/GRC reviews and may request remediation plan. 3. Approval: Exceptions are approved by the Risk Board (security, legal, product) or escalated to CTO for high-risk items. 4. Monitoring: Approved exceptions require metrics/alerts and a mandatory mid-term review.
Required fields for exception requests:
- risk_summary, business_justification, affected_services, proposed_mitigations, owner, requested_ttl (max 90 days for privileged infra exceptions).

Examples of compensating controls:
- Enhanced monitoring & 1-minute alerting for privilege-elevation activities.
- Network micro-segmentation and IP allow-listing for exceptions involving outbound data flows.

9) Roles, Ownership, and Contact Matrix
- Security (policy, evidence review, incident lead): security@redwood.example.com
- Eng-SRE (logging, runbooks, incident ops): sre-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Eng-Platform (IAM integration, access controls): platform-team@redwood.example.com
- Legal/GRC (contracts, data residency obligations): legal-grc@redwood.example.com

Appendix: Quick runbooks and commands
- Export access review (example):
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${EVIDENCE_TOKEN}' \n    'https://evidence.internal.redwood/api/access-reviews?year=2027' \n  > access-review-2027-06.csv

- Pull audit logs (example):
  gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND severity>=ERROR' --project redwood-prod --limit 1000 --format json > errors-2027-06-01.json
